discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological insulator, characterised by a Z2 invariant, with helical edge states protected against backscattering. Molenkamp's group then grew high-quality HgTe/CdTe quantum wells and observed the quantum spin Hall effect in 2007. That observation, made possible by years of materials control, was the first experimental proof of a topological insulator phase. These works turned band topology from a curiosity of the quantum Hall effect into a general principle of electronic materials. They led to three-dimensional topological insulators, topological superconductivity, the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological films, and new routes to dissipationless electronics and fault-tolerant quantum information. Few ideas in modern condensed matter physics have been so clearly predicted, so decisively confirmed, and so widely influential across laboratories worldwide.
